articles.headline: Germany may get its first woman president
body: Ilse Aigner, a conservative politician from Bavaria, is now the candidate with the best chance of becoming Germany's next president. Chancellor Friedrich Merz *endorses* her. If she wins, she will be the first woman to *hold the office*.
Germans do not elect their president themselves. A special *assembly*, the Federal Convention, votes on 30 January 2027. Frank-Walter Steinmeier, the *incumbent*, has to leave after two *terms*.

quiz.explain: To endorse someone is to say in public that you support them. A chancellor cannot appoint a president.

quiz.sentence: If she wins, she will be the first woman to hold the office.
quiz.explain: Office here means an official position, not a room with desks. To hold it is to have that position.

quiz.sentence: A special assembly, the Federal Convention, votes on 30 January 2027.
quiz.explain: An assembly is a group of people who meet to decide something. The vote is what they do, not what they are.

quiz.sentence: Frank-Walter Steinmeier, the incumbent, has to leave after two terms.
quiz.explain: The incumbent is the person who holds an office right now. Steinmeier is a president, but the word does not mean president.

quiz.sentence: Frank-Walter Steinmeier, the incumbent, has to leave after two terms.
quiz.explain: A term is the fixed time someone may stay in an office. For a German president, one term lasts five years.

articles.headline: SPD leader wants faster reforms from his partner
body: Lars Klingbeil, the SPD leader and finance minister, is putting *pressure* on his coalition partner, the CDU/CSU. He says several reforms that both sides *agreed on* in July are still waiting. He names two: a law on heart health and guaranteed *appointments* with specialist doctors.
The two parties *govern* together, and their leaders meet regularly in a coalition committee to *settle* arguments. The next meeting is coming up soon.

quiz.sentence: Lars Klingbeil, the SPD leader and finance minister, is putting pressure on his coalition partner, the CDU/CSU.
quiz.explain: To put pressure on someone is to push them to act. Blame would mean saying that something is their fault.

quiz.sentence: He says several reforms that both sides agreed on in July are still waiting.
quiz.explain: To agree on something is to decide it together. To argue about it is the opposite.

quiz.sentence: He names two: a law on heart health and guaranteed appointments with specialist doctors.
quiz.explain: An appointment is a fixed time to see someone, such as a doctor. The treatment is what happens once you are there.

quiz.sentence: The two parties govern together, and their leaders meet regularly in a coalition committee to settle arguments.
quiz.explain: To govern is to run a country. Parties negotiate before they govern, and often while they do.

quiz.sentence: The two parties govern together, and their leaders meet regularly in a coalition committee to settle arguments.
quiz.explain: To settle an argument is to end it with a decision that both sides accept.

articles.headline: Parliament passes a new law for the secret services
body: The Bundestag has *passed* a broad reform of the law on Germany's intelligence services. Alexander Dobrindt, speaking for the government, said the country is a *target* of hybrid *threats*. That means attacks that mix spying, sabotage and false information.

Germany has three federal intelligence services: one works *abroad*, one inside the country, and one protects the armed forces. Their powers are limited by law, so every change needs a *majority* in parliament.

quiz.sentence: The Bundestag has passed a broad reform of the law on Germany's intelligence services.
quiz.explain: When a parliament passes a law, it votes yes. If it votes no, it rejects the law.

quiz.sentence: Alexander Dobrindt, speaking for the government, said the country is a target of hybrid threats.
quiz.explain: A target is what an attack is aimed at. The source would be where the attack comes from.

quiz.sentence: Alexander Dobrindt, speaking for the government, said the country is a target of hybrid threats.
quiz.explain: A threat is a danger that may come. An attack is the moment it really happens.

quiz.sentence: Germany has three federal intelligence services: one works abroad, one inside the country, and one protects the armed forces.
quiz.explain: Abroad means in other countries. All three services work in secret, so that word would not tell them apart.

quiz.sentence: Their powers are limited by law, so every change needs a majority in parliament.
quiz.explain: A majority is more than half of the votes. A debate is only the talking before the vote.
